G2-MED-03.lead_in: What is the most appropriate next step in his management?
G2-MED-03.stem: A 64-year-old man is brought to the emergency department 90 minutes after the sudden onset of crushing retrosternal pain with nausea and sweating. His blood pressure is 84/56 mmHg and his heart rate is 58 beats per minute. His jugular venous pressure is elevated to 8 cm above the sternal angle and his lung fields are clear throughout on auscultation. The electrocardiogram shows 3 mm of ST-segment elevation in leads II, III and aVF with reciprocal ST depression in I and aVL. High-sensitivity troponin is 480 ng/L on arrival and 2,900 ng/L on the repeat sample drawn one hour later. The interventional team has been activated and the catheterisation laboratory will be ready to receive him in 25 minutes.

G2-PED-01.lead_in: What is the most likely diagnosis?
G2-PED-01.stem: A 7-month-old girl is brought to the emergency department because of noisy breathing that started today. For the past three days she has had a runny nose, a cough and a temperature up to 37.9 degrees Celsius. This is the first time she has ever wheezed. She has eczema and her mother has asthma. Her respiratory rate is 56 breaths per minute and her oxygen saturation is 95 per cent in room air. There is subcostal indrawing, with widespread expiratory wheeze and crackles, and air entry at the right base is reduced compared with the left.

G2-PED-02.lead_in: Which assessment is most appropriate for this infant on the ward?
G2-PED-02.stem: A 5-month-old boy was admitted to the paediatric ward yesterday with bronchiolitis, on the fourth day of an illness that began with coryza, cough and fever. Overnight his oxygen saturation fell to 89 per cent in room air and low-flow oxygen by nasal prongs was started. This morning his work of breathing and his feeding are much the same as they were on admission rather than better. The ward is full, and the bed manager needs to know whether he can be cohorted in a bay with the other infants who have already tested positive for respiratory syncytial virus.

G2-SURG-02.lead_in: What is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?
G2-SURG-02.stem: A 41-year-old man has had 24 hours of right lower quadrant pain with anorexia and one episode of vomiting. His temperature is 37.4 degrees Celsius and his white cell count is 11.2 x 10^9/L. There is tenderness in the right lower quadrant but no guarding and no rebound. After assessing him the surgical resident judges the probability of appendicitis to be intermediate: not low enough to send him home and not high enough to take him to the operating room. He has normal renal function and no allergies. Both computed tomography and ultrasonography are available in the department without delay.

G2-PSY-03.lead_in: Which initial treatment should be offered?
G2-PSY-03.stem: A 34-year-old woman describes two months of low mood, loss of interest in things she used to enjoy, early morning waking and difficulty concentrating. She has stopped going to her book club and has fallen behind at work, although she is still attending. On assessment she has no thoughts of harming herself and no plan or intent, and she has good support from her partner and her sister. Her physician assesses the episode as of moderate severity. She lives in a rural community where the nearest in-person structured psychotherapy service has a waiting list of more than a year and no therapist practises locally.

G2-PHELO-01.lead_in: Which explanation best accounts for this pattern of results?
G2-PHELO-01.stem: A trial randomly allocated 60,000 adults either to be invited to a screening programme for a solid tumour or to usual care. The two groups were comparable at baseline in age, sex and smoking history. After twelve years of follow-up, median survival measured from the date of diagnosis was 5.8 years among those diagnosed in the invited group and 3.1 years among those diagnosed in the usual-care group. Over the same period there were 412 deaths from the tumour in the invited group and 419 in the usual-care group, a difference the investigators report as not statistically significant.

G2-PHELO-02.lead_in: Which revision to the letter would best protect the autonomy of the people invited?
G2-PHELO-02.stem: A provincial screening programme is revising the letter it sends to invite people to a first screening test. The programme's steering committee has recorded that the purpose of the revision is to help each person invited make the decision that is right for them, and explicitly not to increase the number who attend. The current letter explains what the test involves and where to attend, and the only thing it says about what the programme achieves is that screening reduces deaths from the disease by 25 per cent.

G2-PHELO-03.lead_in: What should the programme do about the planned launch?
G2-PHELO-03.stem: A regional health authority is four weeks away from launching a population screening programme for a treatable cancer. The programme has written goals, a defined target population, and an evaluation plan with agreed indicators and a first report due at eighteen months. The single specialist centre that would perform the confirmatory diagnostic procedure has no additional capacity and its current wait is nine months, and the two surgeons who would treat screen-detected disease are already fully booked, with no further staff or operating time identified anywhere in the region.
